questions: Does the sensor overlap (10 mm spacing, 12 mm footprint) give a smooth enough signal for the Integrator to use kd without amplifying noise?
Is the 50 mm forward offset too far ahead for the controller to react, or does it leave the robot with too little lead at speed?
Does 0.6 kg with a 0.03 m wheel reach the speed needed to finish under 3 s, or is top speed a constraint?
Which track (oval, s-bend, slalom) shows the largest max_error or line loss, and does that point to sensor coverage or to body/track geometry?

intent: Establish a symmetric, well-overlapped five-sensor baseline with sensor weights proportional to sensor x, a moderate wheel track and radius for responsive turning, and a light mass for acceleration. Use it as a reference point: the Integrator's tuning feedback and the first race will show whether sensor spacing, forward offset and mass are the limiting factors before I change them.
learning: Baseline only. Next iteration, if the race shows line loss on sharp bends, I will widen the sensor array (for example to 0.04 m total span) or increase sensor_size. If the robot is too slow, I will reduce mass or increase wheel radius. If the signal is noisy, I will reduce sensor count or shrink the footprint to improve contrast.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or integration feedback yet. I am starting from a conservative, symmetric platform that a controller can be built on. Five sensors at 10 mm spacing, each 12 mm square, overlap enough that the tape (25 mm wide) always covers at least one sensor and the reading varies smoothly as the robot drifts. The sensors sit 50 mm ahead of the axle so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it. Sensor x positions are proportional to the steering weights ([-2,-1,0,1,2] scaled to x), so the sign convention is consistent: a robot drifting left sees the line under the right-hand sensors and gets a negative (steer-right) signal. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn rate and a top speed that can plausibly reach the 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s. Mass 0.6 kg keeps acceleration and braking responsive while still being realistic for the drivetrain. Body width 0.12 m gives a comfortable off-track margin (about 0.043 m from the centre line). I expect the robot to complete the oval and s-bend, with the slalom being the most likely place to show line loss or oscillation. The main unknowns are the sensor spacing relative to the tape and whether the mass and wheel size limit top speed.
